title: feat: simplify model pricing list
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes the obsolete model sorting state, URL parameters, and clickable generation header.
- Changes the default from generations-per-Pollen sorting to the curated order returned by the public model catalog, without client-side reordering.
- Shows each estimate as a two-line `gen per pollen` value on desktop and mobile.
- Labels only explicitly free models as free and adds specific tooltips for free and unavailable usage data.
- Adds a compact explanation of the rolling 7-day usage estimate.

The previous card layout retained a single sortable column after its other headers disappeared, leaving sorting behavior without a complete visible control.

Checks:
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npx vitest run test/model-calculations.test.ts test/model-categories.test.ts`
- Browser verification for finite, free, and unavailable states

gist.headline: The model shelf got tidy
gist.blurb: The model list stopped pretending one lonely number was a whole sorting interface. It now follows the catalog’s curated order, with usage estimates that explain themselves.
gist.summary: Simplified the public model pricing list by removing obsolete URL-based sorting, preserving the curated catalog order, and displaying rolling 7-day generation estimates as two-line “gen per pollen” values with clear free and unavailable-state tooltips.
gist.impact: Users can scan models in the intended catalog order and understand whether an estimate is free, available, or still being calculated without relying on a leftover sortable header.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden librarian with tiny reading glasses, arranging labeled seed packets on a cozy curated shelf rather than sorting them with a broken lever. Each packet represents a model and has a small two-line generation-per-Pollen label; a retro terminal explains the rolling 7-day estimate, while flowers and code-plants make the catalog feel like a well-tended garden.
